text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging: Elevated DNS resolver error rates observed from ap-southeast-1 (APAC edge). 30% of queries to external resolvers returning SERVFAIL since 01:04 UTC. Auto-alert threshold breached.

maria (oncall): seeing it too, dashboards show spike in 5xx for /infer endpoints in apac. High latency for users in SG/HK. Can someone triage upstream resolvers? @nate can you take? :eyes:

nate: on it. initial look shows a surge of NX/SERVFAIL from our egress to Cloudflare public resolvers (1.1.1.1) and some timeouts to a subset of Route53 resolvers. not global — mostly ap-southeast for first 5 min then widening.

ivan: adding context — we rolled a small geo-routing tweak to improve latency at 00:50 UTC that changed resolver priority order (CF first -> Route53 fallback). could be correlated.

maria (oncall): rollback that geo routing change? do we have canary rollback in place?

nate: rolling back now. patch ID: geo-egress-priority-2026-03-15-004. invoking deploy-bot.

cloudops-bot: deploy started by @nate — rollback geo-egress-priority-2026-03-15-004 to previous policy.

support-eng: customers reporting errors: a few commute apps in SG show 502s and failed auth calls. opening a support incident for top 5 customers.

maria (oncall): while rollback runs, can we run quick diagnostics from an affected edge? paste dig results and packet capture if possible.

nate: dig from ap-southeast edge to 1.1.1.1:
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> @1.1.1.1 example.com A +time=5 +tries=1
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
```
And to a Route53 resolver IP (203.0.113.45):
```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> @203.0.113.45 example.com A +time=4 +tries=1
;; WARNING: recursion requested but not available
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345
```

ivan: interesting — TTLs and cached answers look fine in other regions. Looks like upstream resolver cluster in apac lost some authoritative paths, maybe BGP flap or rate-limited queries.

maria (oncall): temporary mitigation: set our resolver fallback to internal authoritative cache (edge-kv-cache) and reduce external resolver fanout to 2. Also enable short-circuit: if external returns SERVFAIL, try origin authoritative directly. Can infra apply policy change?

nate: applying policy change to ap-southeast edges: set extern_resolver_fanout=2, enable origin_fallback=true. patch applied to pool-edge-apac-1.

cloudops-bot: config update success on pool-edge-apac-1.

maria (oncall): good, metrics showing error rate dropping from 30% -> 8% in 90s. still some customer impact but much improved. keep rollback in progress for the geo routing change.

ivan: rollback confirmed complete. geo routing reverted to previous resolver priority.

support-eng: customer notes: 4 customers had transient errors for ~7-12 minutes. we emailed incident notifications with link to status page.

maria (oncall): next steps: 1) monitor for 30m, 2) open ticket with Cloudflare + AWS Route53 with query logs attached, 3) run canary tests across APAC zones, 4) postmortem if trend recurs. I'll take owner for incident postmortem.

nate: collecting pcap and query logs, uploading to S3: s3://redwood-incident-logs/5187654321/  — will attach dig traces and timestamps.

cloudops-bot: external provider ticket created: CF ticket #CF-20260315-APAC-FANOUT, AWS case #1234567890 (refer to S3 bundle).

maria (oncall): customer impact summary for RCA draft: "Intermittent resolver failures from external providers in APAC caused elevated DNS SERVFAILs and timeouts; a recent geo-egress priority change increased exposure to the affected resolver cluster, amplifying impact. Mitigation included rollback of geo-egress change, limiting external resolver fanout, and enabling authoritative origin fallback. Approx 4-12 minutes of degraded service for affected customers; no data loss. Postmortem planned."

ivan: quick note — consider adding probe-based circuit breaker for resolver latency and hit a hard failover faster next time. Also add route-level health probes in LB for CF vs Route53 to avoid prioritized routing to degraded resolver sets.

maria (oncall): agreed. action items recorded. thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident resolved (status: degraded -> mitigated). Duration: ~14 minutes. Handing off to postmortem channel.

nate: final: running extended canary, all green for 20m. I'll keep a watch for 2 hours and then clear on-call.

support-eng: support notifications sent, scheduled follow-up calls with two impacted customers.

maria (oncall): closing thread, will file postmortem with timeline and follow-ups.
